column1: quantity|How much of something there is.|We measured the quantity of water in the jug.
quarter|One of four equal parts.|I ate a quarter of the apple.
quicker|Taking less time than something else.|The bus was quicker than walking.
quickest|Taking the least time of all.|This was the quickest route to school.
quite|Fairly, or to a noticeable amount.|The puzzle was quite tricky.
rabbit|A small furry animal with long ears.|The rabbit nibbled a carrot.
race|A contest to see who finishes first.|We ran a race across the field.
ravi's|Belonging to someone called Ravi.|Ravi's kite flew above the trees.
re-enter|To go into a place again.|We can re-enter the hall after lunch.
read|To look at written words and understand them.|I read a story to my little sister.
reappear|To become visible again.|The sun will reappear when the cloud moves.
reasonable|Fair and sensible.|Taking turns is a reasonable way to share.
receive|To get something that is given or sent.|I will receive a letter from my cousin.
recent|Happening not long ago.|Our recent trip to the farm was fun.
recommend|To say that something is worth choosing.|I recommend this funny book.
redecorate|To change the paint or decorations in a room.|We will redecorate the bedroom with yellow paint.
redo|To do something again.|I need to redo the last part of my drawing.
referee|Someone who makes sure players follow the rules.|The referee blew a whistle to start the match.
reference|Something you look at for information.|I used a map for reference when drawing the island.
referral|Sending someone to another person for help.|The doctor made a referral to an eye specialist.
referred|Sent someone for help, or mentioned something.|The teacher referred to the chart on the wall.
referring|Mentioning or pointing to something.|I was referring to the red book on the shelf.
refresh|To make something feel fresh or new again.|A cool drink will refresh us after our walk.
regular|Happening often or at even times.|Our dog needs regular walks.
reign|The time when a king or queen rules.|We learnt about a queen's long reign.
rein|A strap used to guide a horse.|The rider held a rein in each hand.
relevant|Connected to what is being discussed.|Choose a picture that is relevant to your story.
reliable|Able to be trusted to do what is needed.|Our reliable clock wakes us each morning.
replied|Gave an answer.|I replied to my friend's letter.
replies|Answers that someone gives.|The teacher read our replies to the question.
reply|To give an answer.|Please reply when I ask your name.
replying|Giving an answer.|She was replying to a question about her painting.
rescue|To save someone or something from danger.|The crew went to rescue the stranded boat.
restaurant|A place where people pay to eat a meal.|We ate noodles at the restaurant.
return|To go or give something back.|Please return the book to the library.
ride|To travel on a bike, animal or vehicle.|I can ride my bike around the park.
right|Correct, or the opposite side from left.|You found the right answer.
road|A route with a firm surface for vehicles.|We crossed the road at the crossing.
rocks|Hard pieces of stone.|We found smooth rocks beside the stream.
rude|Speaking or behaving without care for others.|It is rude to push in front of someone.
rule|An instruction that tells you what is allowed.|Our first rule is to take turns.
runner|Someone who runs.|The runner stopped for a drink of water.
runny|Thin and able to flow easily.|The paint was too runny to stay on the brush.
sacrifice|Giving up something important to help someone or achieve a goal.|Giving up her turn was a sacrifice to help her friend.
sadder|Feeling more unhappy.|The lost puppy looked sadder when it began to rain.
saddest|Feeling the most unhappy.|This was the saddest part of the story.
sadly|In an unhappy way.|The child waved sadly as the train left.
sadness|The feeling of being unhappy.|A hug helped ease my sadness.
safe|Protected from danger.|My helmet helps keep my head safe.
same|Exactly alike, or not different.|We both chose the same book.
saw|Looked at something in the past.|I saw a fox beside the hedge.
say|To speak words.|Please say your name clearly.
scared|Feeling afraid.|The kitten was scared of the loud thunder.
scene|A place or part of a story or play.|The first scene takes place in a garden.
scheme|A plan for doing something.|Our school has a scheme to help us recycle.
science|Learning about the world by observing and testing ideas.|In science we tested which objects float.
score|The number of points in a game or test.|Our final score was ten points.
sea|A large area of salty water.|The boat sailed across the sea.
secretary|Someone who helps organise messages and other work.|The school secretary answered the phone.
section|One part of a larger thing.|This section of the book is about birds.
see|To notice something using your eyes.|I can see a rainbow through the window.
seen|Noticed something with your eyes.|Have you seen my blue pencil?
sensation|A feeling in your body.|The cold water gave my toes a tingling sensation.
sensible|Showing good judgement and care.|Wearing a coat in the rain is sensible.
sensibly|In a way that shows good judgement.|We sensibly waited for the rain to stop.
serial|A story told in several separate parts.|We listened to a radio serial about a lost dragon.
serious|Important or needing careful attention.|The teacher gave us a serious warning about the icy path.
share|To let others use or have part of something.|I will share my coloured pencils with you.
she|A word used instead of a girl's or woman's name.|She carried her book into the classroom.
shiny|Reflecting light brightly.|The shiny spoon sparkled in the sunlight.
shirt|A piece of clothing for the top half of your body.|My shirt has a pocket on the front.
shore|The land at the edge of a sea or lake.|We collected shells along the shore.
short|Not long or not tall.|We took a short walk before tea.
shoulder|The part of your body where your arm joins your side.|A butterfly landed on my shoulder.
show|To let someone see something.|Please show me your painting.
side|One of the edges or surfaces of something.|Write your name on this side of the paper.
signature|Your name written in your own special way.|The author put her signature inside my book.
simply|In an easy or plain way.|The teacher explained the task simply.
sincere|Meaning what you say and being honest about it.|He gave a sincere thank you for the help.
sincerely|In an honest way that shows you mean it.|I sincerely hope your kitten feels better soon.
sketch|A quick drawing with few details.|I made a sketch of the tree.
skin|The outer covering of your body.|Sunscreen helps protect your skin.
so|A word that can show what happens as a result.|It was cold, so I put on my coat.
soil|The earth in which plants grow.|We planted seeds in the damp soil.
soldier|Someone who serves in an army.|The soldier helped carry supplies after the flood.
solemn|Very serious and quiet.|Everyone was solemn during the quiet ceremony.
son|Someone's male child.|Her son likes building model boats.
soon|After a short time.|The bus will be here soon.
sound|Something you can hear.|I heard the sound of birds singing.
spends|Uses money or time for something.|She spends an hour reading each evening.
spontaneous|Happening naturally without being planned.|We had a spontaneous dance in the kitchen.
squash|To press something until it becomes flatter.|Do not squash the flowers in your bag.
squirrel|A small animal with a long bushy tail.|The squirrel carried a nut up the tree.
start|To begin doing something.|We will start the game after lunch.
station|A place where trains stop for passengers.|We waited at the station for our train.
stationary|Staying still in one place.|The train remained stationary beside the platform.
stationery|Things used for writing, such as paper and pens.|The shop sells stationery for school.
stay|To remain in a place.|Please stay beside me on the busy pavement.
steal|To take something without permission.|The cheeky gull tried to steal my sandwich.
steel|A strong metal made mainly from iron.|The bridge has strong steel beams.
stomach|The part inside your body that helps break down food.|My stomach rumbled before lunch.
subdivide|To split something into smaller parts.|We can subdivide each square into four triangles.
subheading|A small heading for one part of a piece of writing.|I added a subheading above the paragraph about food.
submarine|A vessel that can travel under water.|The submarine moved beneath the waves.
submerge|To put something completely under water.|We watched the toy submarine submerge in the bath.
substance|A material that something is made of.|The sticky substance on my hands was glue.
substantial|Large or important in size or amount.|We made substantial progress on our class model.
sufficient|As much as is needed.|We have sufficient paper for everyone to draw.
suggest|To offer an idea for someone to think about.|I suggest we read a story before bed.
summer|The warmest season of the year.|We enjoy long sunny days in summer.
sunk|Gone down below the surface of water.|The pebble had sunk to the bottom of the pond.
sunset|The time when the sun disappears below the horizon.|The sky turned pink at sunset.
superman|An imaginary man with amazing powers.|In his story, a superman could lift a mountain.
supermarket|A large shop selling food and other things.|We bought apples at the supermarket.
superstar|Someone who is very famous and successful.|The singer became a superstar.
suppose|To think something is likely, without being sure.|I suppose the picnic will be indoors if it rains.
suspicious|Thinking that something may be wrong or untrue.|The cat was suspicious of its new toy.
symbol|A picture or mark that stands for something.|A heart is often used as a symbol of love.
system|Parts that work together in an organised way.|Our library has a system for sorting books.
table|A piece of furniture with a flat top and legs.|We sat at the table to eat lunch.
take|To carry or move something with you.|Please take your coat to school.
talk|To speak with someone.|We can talk about the story together.
temperature|How hot or cold something is.|We measured the temperature of the water.
tension|A tight feeling, or a feeling of worry.|There was tension as we waited for the race to start.
term|One part of the school year.|We are learning about plants this term.
terrible|Very bad.|The terrible weather kept us indoors.
terribly|Very much, or in a very bad way.|I was terribly excited about our trip.
thanks|A word used to show you are grateful.|I said thanks when my friend helped me.
the|A word used before a particular person or thing.|Please close the door quietly.
theme|The main idea of something.|The theme of our class display is the ocean.
therefore|For that reason.|It was raining; therefore, we wore our waterproof coats.
these|A word for more than one thing nearby.|These apples are ready to eat.
they|A word used instead of the names of people or things.|They played together in the garden.
thief|Someone who takes things without permission.|The story's thief returned the stolen crown.
think|To use your mind to have ideas or understand something.|I think the answer is seven.
third|Coming after second.|I finished third in the sack race.
thistle|A plant with prickly leaves and often purple flowers.|A bee landed on the purple thistle.
thorough|Careful and complete.|We gave the muddy boots a thorough clean.
those|A word for more than one thing further away.|Those birds are flying towards the trees.
threw|Sent something through the air with your hand.|I threw the ball to my friend.
thunder|The loud rumbling sound during a storm.|We heard thunder after the flash of lightning.
thursday|The day after Wednesday.|Our class visits the library on Thursday.
tie|To fasten something with a knot.|I can tie my own shoelaces.
time|What we measure in seconds, minutes and hours.|There is time for one more story.
tinsel|Shiny strips used as decorations.|We hung silver tinsel around the window.
to|A word that can show where someone or something is going.|We walked to the park.
toe|One of the small parts at the end of your foot.|I wiggled each toe in the sand.
told|Said something to someone in the past.|Grandad told us a funny story.
tolerable|Possible to put up with, even if not pleasant.|Opening a window made the heat tolerable.
tolerably|In a way that is fairly good or possible to put up with.|With a cushion, the hard seat was tolerably comfortable.
tolerance|Accepting differences or putting up with something difficult.|We show tolerance by respecting other people's beliefs.
tolerant|Accepting people who are different from you.|A tolerant friend respects your different ideas.
toleration|Allowing something even if you do not like it.|Toleration of different opinions helps us work together.
tongue|The soft part in your mouth that helps you taste and speak.|My tongue turned purple after eating berries.
too|Also, or more than is needed.|I would like to play too.
took|Carried or moved something in the past.|I took my drawing home.
touch|To put your hand or another body part on something.|Please do not touch the wet paint.
towards|In the direction of something.|The puppy ran towards its ball.
towel|A piece of cloth used to dry things.|I dried my hands on a clean towel.
town|A place with homes, shops and streets.|We went into town to visit the library.
transference|Moving something from one place or person to another.|The transference of pollen helps some plants make seeds.
transferred|Moved something to another place.|We transferred the seedlings into bigger pots.
transferring|Moving something to another place.|We are transferring our pictures to a new folder.
travel|To go from one place to another.|We travel to school by bus.
tremendous|Very large or very great.|The crowd gave a tremendous cheer.
tried|Made an effort to do something.|I tried to balance on one foot.
tries|Makes an effort to do something.|She tries her best at every game.
trouble|A problem or difficulty.|I had trouble opening the stiff lid.
true|Correct or really happening.|The story about our lost cat was true.
try|To make an effort to do something.|I will try to finish this puzzle.
tube|A long hollow object.|We rolled a marble through a cardboard tube.
tuesday|The day after Monday.|We have swimming lessons on Tuesday.
tune|A set of musical notes that make a melody.|I hummed a cheerful tune.
tunnel|A passage through or under something.|The train went through a dark tunnel.
turn|To move around or change direction.|Turn left at the next gate.
twelfth|Coming after eleventh.|She opened the twelfth door on the calendar.
under|Below something.|The cat slept under the table.
understandable|Easy to understand, or making sense in the situation.|Your worry about starting a new school is understandable.
undo|To open or reverse something that was done.|Please undo the knot in this ribbon.
unfair|Not treating everyone equally or properly.|It would be unfair to take two turns.
unhappy|Feeling sad or not pleased.|The puppy looked unhappy without its toy.
unique|The only one of its kind.|Every snowflake has a unique pattern.
unload|To take things out of a vehicle or container.|We helped unload the shopping from the car.
unlock|To open a lock or make something available.|This key will unlock the garden gate.
use|To do something with an object or tool.|We use a ruler to draw straight lines.
usual|Happening most of the time.|We sat in our usual places for lunch.
usually|Most of the time.|I usually walk to school with my sister.
valley|Low land between hills or mountains.|A river flowed through the valley.
variety|Several different kinds of something.|We planted a variety of flowers.
various|Several different kinds.|There were various games to choose from.
vegetable|A plant or part of a plant that we eat.|A carrot is a crunchy vegetable.
vehicle|Something used to carry people or things.|The rescue vehicle had bright flashing lights.
vein|A tube carrying blood towards your heart.|I can see a blue vein beneath my skin.
verb|A word that often tells us about an action or state.|Run is a verb because it names an action.
vicious|Deliberately cruel or likely to cause harm.|The vicious dragon frightened everyone in the story.
vigorous|Strong and full of energy.|A vigorous shake mixed the paint.
village|A small group of homes, usually in the countryside.|Our village has a little shop and a school.
visible|Able to be seen.|The moon was visible above the trees.
visibly|In a way that can be seen.|The puppy was visibly excited by its new toy.
wait|To stay until something happens.|Please wait until the light turns green.
walk|To move along on your feet.|We walk through the park every morning.
wander|To walk around without a fixed route.|We like to wander along the woodland paths.
war|Fighting between countries or large groups.|Our history book explains how the war ended.
wary|Being careful because there might be danger.|The fox was wary of the noisy dog.
watch|To look at something carefully for a time.|We can watch the birds from the window.
way|A route or a method of doing something.|This path is the way to the pond.
we|A word for yourself and other people together.|We planted beans in the school garden.
wear|To have clothes or accessories on your body.|I wear a warm coat in winter.
weary|Very tired.|The weary walkers rested on a bench.
weather|What the air and sky are like outside.|The sunny weather was perfect for our picnic.
week|A period of seven days.|We have a spelling test each week.
weigh|To find out how heavy something is.|We will weigh the flour before baking.
well|In a good way, or feeling healthy.|You played that tune very well.
wheel|A round part that turns to help something move.|The cart has a wooden wheel on each side.
when|A word used to ask or tell at what time.|When does our train leave?
whether|A word used when there is a choice between possibilities.|I cannot decide whether to draw a cat or a dog.
while|During the time that something else happens.|I read a book while the cake cooled.
who|A word used to ask or tell which person.|Who left this scarf on the bench?
who's|A short way of saying who is or who has.|Who's coming to the park with us?
whole|All of something, with no part missing.|We spent the whole afternoon building a den.
whose|A word asking or telling who something belongs to.|Whose coat is hanging by the door?
wild|Living or growing without being looked after by people.|A wild rabbit hopped across the field.
winter|The coldest season of the year.|We wear gloves in winter.
woke|Stopped sleeping.|I woke when the birds began to sing.
woman|An adult female person.|The woman at the library helped me find a book.
women|More than one woman.|Two women were planting flowers in the park.
won|Came first or succeeded in a contest.|Our team won the quiz.
wood|The hard material inside the trunk and branches of a tree.|This chair is made of wood.
word|Letters or sounds that have a meaning.|I learnt a new word in my book.
wore|Had clothes or accessories on in the past.|I wore my red boots in the snow.
work|To do a job or spend effort on something.|We work together to tidy the classroom.
world|The Earth and all the places and living things on it.|Our world has many different habitats.
worm|A small long animal with a soft body and no legs.|A worm wriggled into the soil.
worth|Having a particular value or deserving something.|This story is worth reading again.
wrap|To cover something by folding material around it.|We will wrap the gift in blue paper.
write|To make letters or words on a surface.|I can write my name in joined-up letters.
written|Put into words on paper or a screen.|I have written a story about a dragon.
wrong|Not correct.|I rubbed out the wrong answer and tried again.
wrote|Made letters or words in the past.|I wrote a postcard to my cousin.
yacht|A boat used for sailing or racing.|The yacht sailed past the harbour.
yawn|To open your mouth wide when tired.|I began to yawn near bedtime.
year|A period of twelve months.|We celebrate a birthday every year.
you|A word used for the person being spoken to.|Would you like to join our game?
young|Not having lived for very long.|The young duck followed its mother.
your|Belonging to the person being spoken to.|Please put your bag on the hook.
zoo|A place where people care for animals that visitors can see.|We saw penguins at the zoo.
